rows.synopsis: It's winter time in Fraggle Rock, and Cantus arrives to help the Fraggles celebrate the Festival of the Bells. However, Gobo's holiday spirits aren't up and he's forgotten the true meaning. So to make this holiday extra special, he decides he's going to find the Great Bell of Fraggle Rock and bring it back before the celebration begins. But the Rock grows colder, and as Red, Mokey, Boober and Wembley wait, they grow closer to becoming frozen. Cantus goes to find Gobo and bring him back, but Gobo's still wanting to bring the Great Bell back. Will he be able to bring the bell back before his friends freeze? Or will he finally understand the true importance of the Festival of the Bells?
rows.situation: Gobo has lost the feeling of the Festival of the Bells, so he sets off to find the Great Bell itself, and learns from Cantus that the heart of the rock is the Fraggles who ring their bells together.
rows.notes: script-verified (Forever Dreaming transcript, identity-checked); content consideration: the waiting Fraggles grow dangerously cold before Gobo returns.

rows.synopsis: Red absolutely loves her radish bars (which are the equivalent of Pop-Tarts in our world). So when she sees that whenever she wakes up from sleeping that her bars are missing, she sets out to find the crook, which leads her to think her roommate Mokey stole them. She also gets Gobo to hide in a hole outside her room to watch and see if it really is Mokey; after Gobo gets distracted from reading a postcard, the bars go missing again, but Gobo claims he didn't see anything. So finally she gets Wembley to stay the night with her to catch the thief, and what Wembley finds ends up being quite surprising.
rows.situation: Red wakes to find her radish bars gone, accuses her roommate Mokey without proof, and discovers she ate them herself in her sleep, then has to own it in front of the whole Rock.
rows.notes: script-verified (Forever Dreaming transcript, identity-checked); content consideration: Red is publicly judged guilty of false accusation; the lesson is to get real proof before accusing anyone, and to apologize.

rows.synopsis: It's Joke Day in Fraggle Rock, and Boober's trying to get out before his friends find him and make him participate in the holiday he hates. But before he leaves, a huge purplish-pink glob rolls into the Great Hall. Boober ends up meeting Cotterpin Doozer as well, and the Doozers are on their way to start building near the Blob. However, the Glob starts to eat the Doozers, one by one, and soon enough, Cotterpin's inside the Glob too. Even though a part of Boober really just wants to run away and pretend it isn't happening, he's forced into action and must find a way to set the Doozers free.
rows.situation: Boober dreads having to be silly in front of everyone on Joke Day and tries to sneak away, until a glob that eats Doozers forces him to choose between hiding and helping, and he learns he can act even when scared.
rows.notes: script-verified (Forever Dreaming transcript, identity-checked); content consideration: the Glob swallows Doozers whole (they are freed unharmed); Boober apologizes to Cotterpin for not helping sooner.

rows.synopsis: Gobo finds the legendary "Grapes of Generosity", mystical fruits which are rumored to compel anyone who eats them to share them with others. However, when Gobo brings them back, he ends up eating them and keeping them all to himself. Before long, Gobo becomes weightless, and tries to hide it from everyone else. But when he hears that Red climbed to the very top of the Great Hall, it's up to him to get Red down safely, and finally admit to everyone that his own problem was caused by being greedy.
rows.situation: Gobo eats the legendary Grapes of Generosity instead of sharing them, floats away weightless, and has to admit his greed out loud to save Red.
rows.notes: script-verified (Forever Dreaming transcript, identity-checked); the grapes are magic and the lesson is sharing.

rows.episode_title: Blanket Of Snow, Blanket Of Woe

But she ends up being too late, and when she sees Philo and Gunge mourning over the frozen Marjorie, she decides she has to fix her mistake. When she overhears the Gorgs need to throw out some yucky, hot soup, she along with the help of Gobo go into the Gorg's castle to find a way to get the soup on the Trash Heap so she can thaw out.

However, Boober's not too fond of the idea, and shares his worries with Wembley along the way. Before long, Wembley comes up with a bad case of the Pebble Pox, too. Will Boober leave his sick friend behind and ditch the journey, or will Boober put his germ-worries aside to help his friends?

rows.synopsis: When Gobo, Red and Wembley are searching for unique items, Wembley comes upon an old green bottle. He takes it back to his cave, and while he's polishing the bottle up, a genie appears. Wembley can hardly believe his luck, but this genie has his own agenda. He destroys all the items Gobo and Red found, then he scares Boober half to death by making his laundry look like ghosts. Gobo says he needs to get rid of the mean genie, but the genie says he needs to stop letting Gobo boss him around. Later on, Wembley decides Gobo was right, and they create a plan to get the genie back in the bottle, then bury it. The plan works, but Wembley feels sorry for the genie, and lets him out. Later on, when Gobo's trying to show everyone the bottle, he accidentally breaks it, but Wembley confesses he let him out. The genie shows up again, and turns all the Fraggles into something that looks like a Fraggle army. It's up to Wembley to stick up for himself to make things right again.
rows.situation: Wembley finds a genie who scares his friends and pushes him around, and he learns the difference between standing up for yourself and just doing whatever you want, using his last wish to set the genie free.

Mokey gets all worked up about this, but when she brings Red back so she can be a Poohbah, Mokey finally learns not to take anything too serious that these Fraggles tell her.

rows.synopsis: Cotterpin Doozer is accused of consorting with Fraggles, and she must prove that Fraggles are noble and intelligent and worthy of the respect of the Doozers.

rows.notes: script-verified (Forever Dreaming transcript, identity-checked); content consideration: trial and expulsion stakes and a baby Cackler grabbing Cotterpin; Large Marvin gives up all his food to save her. No controlled topic fits.

rows.synopsis: When Fraggle Rock's water supply is contaminated by the Silly Creatures, only Boober can save the day.
rows.situation: The Fraggle water supply turns bitter, and Boober, the Fraggle nobody listens to, is the only one who smells it in time, while Doc turns down one hundred thousand dollars to store waste under his house.
rows.notes: script-verified (Forever Dreaming transcript, identity-checked); content consideration: industrial waste contamination of drinking water, resolved by a fresh-water flush; no controlled topic fits the environmental story.

rows.synopsis: Red and Gobo's swimming competition is interrupted by the annual arrival of the Knobblies, pink vine-like plants which are particularly thick this year, and which turn out to lead to something quite unexpected.
rows.situation: Red and Gobo's swimming contest ends when the year's thick Knobblies drag them under the pond to the Merggles, and the discovery that the roots connect everyone turns rivals' bickering into a new friendship.
rows.notes: script-verified (Forever Dreaming transcript, identity-checked); content consideration: the Fraggles are pulled underwater and panic before the Merggles appear; the swim competition is the story's entry frame, so the topic tag is defensible but partial. No coping value fits the resolution.

rows.synopsis: On his first solo overnight hike, Wembley meets Mudwell the Mudbunny, whose behavior first entertains, and then confuses him.
rows.situation: On Wembley's first solo overnight hike he befriends Mudwell the Mudbunny, whose strange behavior turns out to be goodbye, and Wembley finds a way to accept losing a friend and keep him in his memory.
rows.notes: script-verified (Forever Dreaming transcript, identity-checked); content consideration: a friend character dies; this is a gentle, honest grief story and the strongest loss episode in the batch; Wembley works it through by talking with Gobo. No controlled topic fits.

rows.synopsis: Mokey, Wembley and Boober get transported back in time, to an era when Fraggles are bald, have leaders, and never laugh.
rows.situation: Mokey, Wembley and Boober are transported back to a Fraggle era of bald, solemn leaders who never laugh, and their silliness proves to be the legend that brings laughter back.
rows.notes: script-verified (Forever Dreaming transcript, identity-checked); content consideration: a stern leader society that punishes laughing; the resolution is comic and legendary rather than a named coping strategy, so coping is left empty.

rows.synopsis: It's Ma and Pa Gorg's 513th anniversary, and they must get married again. But where's the ring?
rows.situation: Pa Gorg forgets his and Ma's 513th anniversary and must marry her all over again, and with Junior smoothing the way the Gorgs learn that saying the words is what keeps love going.
rows.notes: script-verified (Forever Dreaming transcript, identity-checked); content consideration: a wedding farce with Gobo briefly offered as the bridal gift; no controlled topic fits.

rows.synopsis: The Fraggle Horn is missing, and Red tries to find it, accusing many along the way.
rows.situation: When the Fraggle horn vanishes, Inspector Red accuses half the Rock before she finds the real culprit, a Fraggle who took it because her nose-bopping at meetings embarrassed and hurt him, and she promises to stop.
rows.notes: script-verified (Forever Dreaming transcript, identity-checked); the lesson is not jumping to conclusions and noticing small unkindnesses; no controlled topic fits.

rows.episode_title: The Gorg Who Would Be King
rows.synopsis: The leaves of the Nirvana tree have fallen, and it's time for Junior Gorg to become king, but not until he has a chance to get a different perspective on the Universe.
rows.situation: The last leaf falls and Junior Gorg becomes king of the universe, and after seeing how well everything runs without being bossed, his first and last royal act is to declare there will be no more king.
rows.notes: script-verified (Forever Dreaming transcript, identity-checked); content consideration: Pa Gorg hurls a comic bomb object in the Gorg scrimmage; the resolution is Junior's own decision, not a coping strategy from the list. No controlled topic fits.

rows.synopsis: Cantus and the Minstrels are back and ready to perform the Song of Songs, but first Gobo must find the Honk of Honks. Along the way, he meets Doc face to face for the first time.
rows.situation: Cantus returns for the Song of Songs and Gobo must find the Honk of Honks, discovering along the way that he and Doc are part of everything, and everything is part of them.
rows.notes: script-verified (Forever Dreaming transcript, identity-checked); content consideration: Doc's subplot mentions Ned's asthma tests; Gobo and Doc meet face to face for the first time.

rows.synopsis: Doc finally knows of the Fraggles, when he and Sprocket have to move. Will Gobo be able to relay the Trash Heap's message ""You cannot leave the magic"" in time?
rows.situation: Doc and Sprocket must move away for Ned's health, and Gobo races to deliver the Trash Heap's last message, that you cannot leave the magic, as the wall between their worlds finally opens.
rows.notes: script-verified (Forever Dreaming transcript, identity-checked); series finale; content consideration: a gentle goodbye and move driven by a friend's illness; the message reframes leaving, which is the shown way of handling the feeling.
